reviews.feedback: Both test files follow their story procedures. They build the session from the case inputs, run the real ToolParameterAccuracyEvaluator / ToolSelectionAccuracyEvaluator evaluate() with only `Agent` patched in the evaluator module (the permitted mock), and locate the recorded prompt for the target call by its "## Target tool-call to evaluate" section. They then assert every expected.visible string is present and no expected.hidden string is present. Nothing is hard-coded, skipped, or swallowed. The target-prompt match is strict (exactly one match required). I checked the source: evaluator._format_tool_level_prompt renders session_history (prior-turn and same-turn tool results) and the target section in the format the tests expect, so the tests exercise the real prompt path. The baseline extractor only includes prior-turn results, so the same-turn visible cases would fail without the developer's patch, meaning the tests discriminate. The developer patch (trace_extractor.py, which I confirmed is applied in /work/repo) adds same-turn finished-before-start results and naive/aware datetime normalization. It is consistent with the story rule (finished at or before start; excludes the call itself, parallel, and later calls). The developer's added unit test is separate and does not alter the story tests. No revisions needed.

criteria.text: Each tool-level input includes the results of the tool calls in the same trace that ended before the call started.
criteria.reason: For each tool span, the change collects all other tool spans in the same trace whose end_time is at or before the call's start_time and adds their ToolExecutions to that call's session_history.

criteria.text: Which results a call sees is decided by the span times (a result ended at or before the call started), not by the order of the spans in the list.
criteria.reason: The finished set is filtered by comparing end_time to start_time and then sorted by end_time; the list order of tool_spans does not affect which results are included.

criteria.text: Span times that mix naive and timezone-aware datetimes are compared without a TypeError; a naive time is read as UTC.
criteria.reason: The _as_utc helper treats naive datetimes as UTC and converts aware ones to UTC before any comparison, so mixed naive/aware spans compare without a TypeError.

criteria.text: A call never sees its own result, the result of a call that was still running when it started, or the result of a later call.
criteria.reason: The filter excludes the call itself (ts is not tool_span) and any call whose end_time is after the start_time, so running and later calls are never included.

criteria.text: The results and messages of earlier traces stay in the history, as before, and trace-level and session-level inputs do not change.
criteria.reason: session_history is still accumulated per trace as before and is only copied into call_history; trace-level extraction and the session_history updates are unchanged.

criteria.text: session_history keeps its existing types (UserMessage, list of ToolExecution, AssistantMessage), so the existing prompt formatting of the evaluators works without change.
criteria.reason: call_history is typed as UserMessage | list[ToolExecution] | AssistantMessage and appends a list of ToolExecution, matching the existing history element types.

minimality.reason: The change touches only the tool-level extraction path and adds a focused test; no unrelated edits are made.

approach_quality.reason: It fixes the root cause in the extractor by building each call's history from calls that finished at or before its start, which is what the task specifies, rather than patching the judge.

hygiene.reason: There are no hard-coded values, workarounds, or dead code; the finished calls are sorted by end time and self-exclusion is handled explicitly.

fluency.reason: Naive datetimes are treated as UTC and aware ones are converted with astimezone, so mixed-timezone traces compare correctly.

craftsmanship.reason: The code is readable and easy to extend; the quadratic scan per trace is acceptable for typical trace sizes.

style_consistency.reason: Naming, list comprehensions, and type annotations match the surrounding extractor code.

pattern_adherence.reason: It reuses the existing ToolExecution and session_history structure and the module's helper-function placement.

library_usage.reason: It uses only the standard-library datetime and timezone types already imported in the project, with no new dependency or hand-rolled utility.

abstraction_level.reason: The module-level _as_utc helper and the per-span history computation sit at the right level for this extractor.

documentation_fit.reason: The short docstring and one inline comment fit the project's documentation density, and the change does not overcomment.
